(a) Lot valuation. The cemetery committee and the city shall place a value upon all unsold lots in the Greenview Cemetery and the Greensboro Cemetery, respectively, and shall record such valuations on an official map or plan of such cemetery. Said map of the Greenview Cemetery shall be kept on file in the office of the cemetery committee, and the map of the Greensboro Cemetery shall be kept on file in the office of the city manager-clerk/treasurer.
(b) Method of purchase. Any person desiring to purchase an easement in a particular lot or lots, for the purpose for which it is intended, shall be permitted to do so upon payment of the fixed price for such lot or upon making arrangements for the purchase of such lot or lots on an installment plan, according to the rules and regulations that may be established by the cemetery committee for the Greenview Cemetery or the city for the Greensboro Cemetery. There shall be no discrimination in the sale of lots on any basis.
(c) Manner of conveying. Conveyances of burial lots shall be executed in the name of the city by the mayor and have affixed thereto the seal of the city. Such conveyance shall not convey fee simple title, but shall convey to the purchaser of the burial lot an easement for the exclusive right of interment and sepulcher in such lot; shall state the maximum number of graves allowed on each such burial lot as shown by the plat; and, by reference therein made, shall convey each lot subject to all of the provisions of this chapter as fully as if set out in such conveyance.
(d) Recordation of deed. At the time the city conveys any burial lot, the cemetery committee (for Greenview Cemetery lots) and the city (for Greensboro Cemetery lots) in addition to collecting the purchase price thereof, shall collect from the purchaser an amount sufficient to have such conveyance so recorded before delivery thereof to the purchaser. No sale or transfer of any such burial lot or any right therein, nor any subdividing of any burial lot by any purchaser or those claiming under him, shall be valid unless approved in writing by the city or until the deed of transfer and such written approval are recorded in the clerk's office, Greene County Superior Court.
(e) Records of ownership. The cemetery committee and the city shall keep full and complete records of the ownership of all lot easements in their respective cemeteries; of the burial capacity of each lot; of the location of each grave, of the names and ages of the persons buried in each grave that has been or shall hereafter be used, and of the date of burial of each.
(f) Sale or transfer by owner. Owners of lots shall not be permitted to sell or transfer lots without the written consent and approval of the cemetery committee, where Greenview Cemetery lots are involved, or the city, where Greensboro Cemetery lots are involved.
(Code 2003, § 24-102)

(a) Location and design. Plans, designs, and locations of all memorial work, including copings, shall be subject to the approval of the cemetery committee, for Greenview Cemetery lots, and the Greensboro Cemetery Association for Greensboro Cemetery lots.
(b) Permit required. Persons erecting or repairing memorials must obtain a permit and, in doing such work, must comply with the reasonable direction of the cemetery committee or the cemetery association. Persons or firms requesting such permit may be required to furnish satisfactory evidence of their ability to perform the work proposed.
(c) First quality material. All monuments, markers, mausoleums, tombs, and copings shall be of first quality granite, marble, or other natural stone suitable for outside memorials. Such material shall be guaranteed by the dealer to be free from sap and components which will cause rust, stains, and natural faults which might cause checks or faults.
(d) Agreement of monument dealers. Monument dealers shall be required to set monuments, markers, and copings in conformity with cemetery requirements and in accordance with the trade standards of proper methods for handling and setting.
(e) Foundations. Foundations for monuments, markers, mausoleums, tombs, and copings shall be installed in accordance with the best trade practices. If any fault resulting from improper installation of foundations develops, the cemetery officials shall require that the condition be remedied promptly and at the cost of the lot owner. Foundations shall be the full size of the base of the memorial and finished one inch below grade on all sides. That part of the foundation below grade must be sufficiently thick and deep to support the size monument being erected for the period of time expected.
(f) First class workmanship. To be considered first class workmanship, a memorial shall not show unsightly point or tool marks or staining from the process of manufacturing.
(g) Base. All bases shall be a rectangular shape, with no indentations or protrusions. They shall be properly finished and installed in accordance with the best trade practices.
(h) Sketch required. To avoid errors, a sketch drawn to scale (unless otherwise permitted) showing design, dimensions, and inscriptions in detail shall be required for submission to the cemetery committee or the cemetery association for approval. Such approval must be procured before commencing work on the memorial.
(i) Right to remove. Should any monument, mausoleum, tomb, or coping become unsightly, dilapidated, or hazardous to visitors, the cemetery committee or the cemetery association shall have the right to correct the condition or remove the entire structure. This work shall be done at the expense of the lot owner.
(j) Workmen. All workmen employed by firms are, while within the cemetery, subject to all reasonable regulations governing the cemetery. Workmen shall keep in their possession a copy of the permit required in subsection (b) of this section while working on the cemetery grounds. No Sunday work shall be permitted.
(k) Tolerances. Dimensional tolerances within reasonable variations from those specified may be allowed; however, differences must be uniform over the whole stone.
(l) Statuary. No freestanding statuary (without foundation) shall be permitted. Some vases and urns shall be permitted. Carved figures in base relief of proper design shall be acceptable.
(m) Clean-up. The lot and surrounding area shall be cleaned by workmen after installation. No excess materials shall be left on or near any work site. Any disposal of excess materials within the cemetery must comply with all directions of the cemetery committee or the cemetery association.
(n) Disposal of pots, flowers, etc. When flower containers, pots, flowers, etc., become unsightly, the cemetery officials shall have the authority to remove them from the premises.
(o) Other instructions. All trucks and heavy equipment must remain on the established roadways within the cemetery. All work must be expeditiously completed. Approval must be secured from cemetery officials before partially completed work may be left in the cemetery for a period exceeding five days. Cemetery officials shall be notified of the completion of all work within the cemetery.
(Code 2003, § 24-104)

Private lands means all real properties lying within the city limits of Greensboro, Georgia, less and except lands hereinafter designated and defined as "public lands."
Public lands means real properties lying between the property lines on either side of all streets, avenues, or ways within the city, all lands owned by the city, and all lands to which the public has free access.
Tree protection means barriers constructed around trees at construction sites sufficient to prevent damage or injury to trunks, limbs, and roots.
Trees means woody perennial plants, either single- or multi-stemmed, commonly exceeding ten feet in height at maturity; shrubs or bushes, and all other woody vegetation on lands lying within the city limits of Greensboro, regardless of size.
(Code 2003, § 27-101)
197:
There is hereby created and established a city tree board for the City of Greensboro, Georgia, which shall consist of the following:
(1) Membership. There shall be appointed seven members by the mayor of Greensboro or his designee. Members shall live in or have a vested interest in the City of Greensboro.
(2) Compensation. Members of the city tree board shall serve without compensation.
(3) Term of office. The term of the seven persons to be appointed by the mayor shall be three years except that the term of two of the members of the first board shall be for two years. In the event that a vacancy should occur during the term of any member, his successor shall be appointed to serve the remainder of the term.
(4) Duties and responsibilities. It shall be the responsibility of the city tree board to study, investigate, counsel, and develop and/or update, and administer a written plan for the care, preservation, pruning, planting, replanting, removal, or disposition of trees and shrubs on public lands within the City of Greensboro. The plan will be presented annually to the city council and upon their acceptance and approval shall constitute the official comprehensive City of Greensboro Tree Plan. The board, when requested by the city council, shall consider, investigate, make finding, report and recommend upon any special matter of question coming within the scope of its work. The city tree board shall also examine plans submitted pursuant to the administrative guidelines and monitor compliance therewith. The city tree board, when requested by the city manager, shall consider, investigate, make findings, report, and recommend upon any special matter or question coming within the scope of its work. Any person dissatisfied with a decision of the city tree board shall have the right, upon proper notice to the city tree board, to request a hearing before the city council, who shall be the ultimate arbiter as to the interpretation and application of this article and the administrative guidelines.
(5) Operation. The city tree board shall elect a chairperson, a vice-chairperson, and a secretary. The secretary shall maintain official minutes of all meetings and proceedings. The city tree board shall meet as often as necessary in regular or special meetings, which shall be called and conducted in accordance with the Georgia Open Meetings Law. A majority of its members shall constitute a quorum for the transaction of business.
(6) List of trees. The tree board shall make a list of desirable and undesirable trees to plant in the city. These should be listed as small, medium and large trees.
(Code 2003, §§ 3-803, 27-102)
198:
On or before March 1 of each year, the city tree board shall draft and recommend administrative guidelines for tree preservation and planting within the City of Greensboro. Said administrative guidelines shall be submitted to the city council for its approval. A public hearing shall be held prior to approval and before any final action on future meetings of this article. Notice of the time, date, and location of the hearing shall be published in the official news organ at least 15 days prior to the hearing. Said administrative guidelines shall provide for the preservation and planting of trees on public lands within the City of Greensboro and all matters relating thereto, including, but not limited to, the requirements for planting and maintaining trees within the city; limitations on paving public lands for driveways or parking; use of pesticides; applications for grading, building, and change of use permitting; and development and similar matters affecting Greensboro's urban forest. The administrative guidelines, when approved as provided for herein, shall be considered as part of this article and be enforceable as such. Upon the failure of the city tree board to submit to the city council a new set of administrative guidelines by March 1 of each year, the existing administrative guidelines shall be considered as the proposed guidelines for the current year.
(Code 2003, § 27-103)
199:
Before any person, corporation, or association plants, removes, destroys, cuts, sprays, or prunes any tree on public land in the City of Greensboro or performs any work or function which results in disturbing, digging into, compaction or displacing of said property, or contracts with another person or corporation to perform such acts, a permit must be obtained from the city. Such permit shall be in addition to all other permits, authorizations, and procedures required by law for work within in disturbing, digging into, compacting, or displacing said property; or contracts with another or along public rights of way, including the state highway system. A written planting plan for the planting, pruning, cutting, removal, or spraying of trees or trenching on public lands must be submitted to the city manager for review by the city tree board prior to any work being performed. The tree board shall approve or deny the plan within ten days of submittal. Any plan not acted upon within ten days shall be deemed approved. All such plans shall conform to this article and the administrative guidelines. Failure to submit such a plan and/or commencing work on public lands without the aforesaid permit shall be considered a violation of this article. If the plan, as submitted, shall be approved by the city tree board, the city manager or his designee shall issue the permit. The city may impose such permit fees as approved from time to time by the city council. Individual permits shall not be required for the City of Greensboro, other licensed public utilities, or the Georgia Department of Transportation, as long as the same adopt and adhere to this article. Public and private utilities which maintain and install overhead and underground utilities, including CATV, water, sewer, etc., shall be required to accomplish all such work on public lands subject to this article to ensure proper pruning and cutting of trees, including protection of roots.
(Code 2003, § 27-105)
200:
(a) Size of landscape strips. The width of a landscape strip must as a minimum be such that a five foot diameter circle fit inside, and be at least 50 square feet total. Excepted are landscape strips that were created on or before March 1, 2003.
(b) Curb and gutter. Curb stops or the like must be used to prevent vehicle overhang into landscape strips or parking islands.
(c) Indemnification. Indemnification and maintenance agreements must be recorded with the Greene County Superior Court Clerk prior to permitting irrigation or plantings within county rights-of-way.
(d) Trees. Trees within landscape strips should be planted to adhere to the following:
(1) Landscape strips 25 feet wide or less shall contain a minimum of one tree for every 30 linear feet of landscape strip.
(2) Landscape strips greater than 25 feet wide shall contain a minimum of one tree for every 20 linear feet of landscape strip.
(3) Trees do not have to be planted in straight lines; clumping is permitted.
(Code 2003, § 27-106)
201:
It shall be unlawful for any person to cut any tree on public lands without obtaining in advance of such cutting, a permit from the city based on a plan approved by the city tree board. The term "cutting" means the removal or cutting back of limbs larger than three inches in diameter from trees or shrubs within the crown to such a degree so as to remove the normal canopy and disfigure the tree. Likewise, it shall be a violation of this article for any person to attach to any trees on public land any rope, wire, chain, signage, or other device.
(Code 2003, § 27-107)
202:
All stumps of trees on public lands shall be removed below the surface of the ground by the city or other authorized entities so that the top of the stump does not project above the surface of the ground.
(Code 2003, § 27-108)
203:
Use of toxic chemicals or herbicides to kill or retard plant growth under concrete or asphalt paving within ten feet of any tree on public lands is prohibited.
(Code 2003, § 27-109)
204:
(a) The City of Greensboro shall have the right to plant, prune, maintain, and remove trees, plants, and shrubs within the lines of all streets, alleys, avenues, and public grounds as may be necessary to ensure public safety or to preserve or enhance the symmetry and beauty of such public lands. The city tree board may remove or order to be removed any tree or part thereof which is in an unsafe condition, or which by reason of its nature in injurious to sewers, electric power lines, gas lines, water lines, or other public improvements, or is affected with any injurious disease, fungus, insect, or other pest.
(b) This section does not prohibit the planting of street trees by adjacent property owners, providing that the selection and location of said trees is in accordance with the other sections of this article.
(Code 2003, § 27-110)
205:
(a) It shall be unlawful as a normal practice for any person, firm, or city department to top any street tree, park tree, or other tree on public land. The term "topping" means the severe cutting back of limbs to stubs larger than three inches in diameter within the tree's crown to such a degree as to remove the normal canopy and disfigure the tree.
(b) Trees severely damaged by storms or other causes, or certain trees under utility wires or other obstructions where other pruning practices are impractical may, after review by the city tree board, be exempted from this article.
(Code 2003, § 27-111)
206:
Every owner of any tree overhanging a street or right-of-way within the City of Greensboro shall prune the branches so that such branches shall not obstruct the light from any street light or obstruct the view of any street intersection, and so that there shall be a clear space of at least eight feet above the surface of the street or sidewalk. Said owners shall remove all dead, diseased, or dangerous trees, or broken or decayed limbs which constitute a menace to the safety of the public. The city shall have the right to prune any tree or shrub on private property when said tree or shrub interferes with the proper spread of light along the street from a street light or interferes the visibility of any traffic control device or sign.
(Code 2003, § 27-112)
207:
The city shall have the right to cause the removal of any dead or diseased trees on private property within the city when such trees constitute a hazard to life and property, or harbor insects or disease which constitutes a potential threat to other trees within the city. The city tree board will notify in writing the owners of said trees. Removal shall be done by said owners at their own expense within 60 days after the date of service of notice. In the event of failure of owners to comply with such provisions, the city shall have the authority to remove such trees and charge the cost of removal to the owners.
(Code 2003, § 27-113)
208:
The provisions of this article shall not apply to private property; however, in addition to landscaping requirements imposed by chapter 121, Zoning, developers and owners of private property are strongly encouraged to promote, develop, and protect the existing urban forest within the City of Greensboro and to use the administrative guidelines in the landscaping of their properties. For those properties abutting the public right-of-way on any street, it is encouraged that plantings be made no closer than 12.5 feet (at maturity) of the right-of-way or any utility easement. Planting is discouraged in areas reserved for drainage easements if such planting would impede or alter the flow of surface waters. For properties abutting upon the intersection of two or more rights-of-way, consideration should be given to plantings which may obstruct the vision of motorists entering such intersection.
(Code 2003, § 27-114)
209:
It shall be unlawful for any person to prevent, delay, or interfere with the city tree board, or any of its agents, which engaging in and about the planting, cultivating, mulching, pruning, spraying, or removing of any street tree, park tree, or trees on private lands as authorized in this article.
(Code 2003, § 27-115)
210:
Any person may appeal any adverse ruling or order of the city tree board to the city manager. If the city manager and the complainant cannot come to agreement, the matter shall be resolved by the city council, who shall hear the matter at it's next regularly scheduled meeting and make a final decision. Any matter not appealed within ten days shall be deemed final. Appeals shall be commenced in writing and filed with the city council, setting forth in sufficient detail the ruling objection and the basis for rejection. Notice of the date, time, and location of the hearing shall be mailed to the appellant via first class mail, certified, return receipt mail at least ten days prior thereto unless the appellant waives said ten-day notice in writing. Hearings shall be conducted in conformity with minimum due process requirements.
(Code 2003, § 27-116)
211:
Violation for the enforcement of the provisions of this article shall be an offense against the city and punishable in the manner provided therefore by citation to the municipal court. Any person violating any provision of this article shall be, upon conviction or plea of guilty, subject to a fine not to exceed $100.00. In addition to any fine imposed, any person or firm violating the same shall:
(1) Bear the costs of replacement and incidentals for the planting of a replacement tree of equal value. Maintenance may be required for two years.
(2) The type of tree, the location of said tree, and the time of planting shall be in conformity with a plan submitted to the city tree board and approved by it.
(Code 2003, § 27-118; Ord. of 6-21-2004)
